explanation: Q1 computes the minimum absolute difference between any two distinct points by considering all pairs (A, B) where A.X != B.X. Q2 computes the minimum difference between consecutive points when sorted by X using the LAG window function. For a set of distinct integers (since X is PRIMARY KEY, ensuring uniqueness), the minimum absolute difference between any two points is always achieved between some consecutive points in the sorted order. This is because for sorted points x1 < x2 < ... < xn, any non-consecutive pair's difference is at least the sum of consecutive differences, and thus cannot be smaller than the minimum consecutive difference. Therefore, under the given schema, Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent and will always return the same result for any valid data.

For example, with points (1, 3, 4), both queries return 1, as the minimum difference is between 3 and 4, which are consecutive when sorted.
